notes: The host owns tab navigation and selects the activeElement.

With sscQueryString set, only a search made from the SSC tab counts as a campaign check; a search from another tab leaves the SSC tab saying the check was not run, with a control to run it. It reaches vehicle-ssc as lookupQueryString, so it never joins a trace request.
The host may use hiddenFields to apply its approved presentation policy.
The current package global script loads shared fonts and browser interop helpers.
Replaces the campaign half of the retired vehicle-warranty-details; warranty coverage is vehicle-warranty-timeline.
Unauthorized campaign lookup and reCAPTCHA configuration are host policy and remain optional raw API properties.
showTrace exposes claim and invoice details per campaign; the host gates it on its own permission check and its endpoint must honour ?trace=ssc.

A lookup-logging flag belongs in lookupQueryString, which joins the lookup request only: the trace request re-reads a lookup already logged and never carries it. The host endpoint must refuse to log traced requests as well (the ADP lookup service does).

Opening a campaign's evidence brings its row to the top of the page and follows the page while the drawer opens; a host whose fixed header covers the top of the page sets scroll-padding-top on its scroll container.
Warranty coverage only. Campaign rendering, reCAPTCHA and unauthorized campaign lookup belong to vehicle-ssc.
claim, completeClaim, activate, claimEndPoint, and document-upload settings are mutation integration features. They remain raw API metadata until their host contract is reviewed.
Takes calendar dates in and gives one out; it makes no requests. A host loads availability on monthChange and passes it back through enabledDates and dayMeta.
Month and weekday names and control labels are bundled for en, ar, ku and ru, so no locale file is fetched.

Rule precedence: range (min/max) → disabledDates → disabledWeekdays → not in enabledDates → isDateDisabled. The first rule that matches is the reason a day is blocked (data-reason on the cell). Rules only ever block: the allow-list never re-enables a day another rule blocked.

Disabled days are focusable but cannot be selected. Inside min/max, the arrow, Home/End and Page keys land on every day of the month, including disabled ones, which carry aria-disabled so a screen-reader user can discover them (the WAI-ARIA APG allows focusable disabled items in composite widgets). Enter and Space do nothing on them. Days of the neighbouring months and days outside min/max are never focused.
A min later than max is an empty range: every day is disabled, the month buttons, Today and the keyboard do not move, and the month stays where it opened unless the host sets month.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-calendar-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline, so host variables win in light and dark. The component never sets --shift-* itself.

Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku — all loaded by the package’s global script. Override with --shift-font-family and --shift-font-family-arabic.

The box never changes size: six rows always, a fixed header band, and the months and years views fill exactly the days view. Only another density (an appearance with a different cell size or gap) or another size resizes it.
Every movement — header roll, day carousel, view slide, year paging — runs on one clock: --shift-calendar-settle (or --shift-settle), 480ms by default; instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

props.value: Selected date as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty. Updated when the user selects a day; a host may set it.
props.month: Month shown in the days view, as YYYY-MM. Settable; clamped to min/max. Opens on the value’s month, else today’s, else the nearest end of the range. Choosing a month or a year in the views moves it.
props.min: Earliest selectable date (inclusive). Navigation stops at its month. A min after max makes the range empty (see the notes).
props.max: Latest selectable date (inclusive). Navigation stops at its month.
props.disabledDates: Dates that cannot be chosen: an array or a comma, space or JSON-array string of YYYY-MM-DD.
props.disabledWeekdays: Weekdays that cannot be chosen, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday: [5, 6], "5,6", "5 6" or "[5,6]".
props.enabledDates: Allow-list. When set (any array, even an empty one) only these dates can be chosen. Null, undefined or an empty string turns it off.
props.isDateDisabled: JS property only. (date) => boolean for any other rule; asked only about days no other rule blocked. A throw counts as disabled.
props.dayMeta: Per-day extras keyed by YYYY-MM-DD: { badge?: short text, tone?: neutral | info | success | warning | danger, description?: read with the date by screen readers }. Badge digits are written in the calendar’s numerals. Object or JSON string.
props.today: YYYY-MM-DD that stands in for today, through ~lib/clock. Empty: the reader’s local calendar date.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Sets names, direction, default week start and digits.
props.weekStartsOn: First column, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday. Default by language: en and ru Monday, ar and ku Saturday.
props.numerals: latn or arab. Default by language: Arabic-Indic digits for ar and ku, Latin for en and ru.
props.label: Accessible name for the calendar group (the field label when used in a form). Default: the localized word for calendar.
props.disabled: Nothing can be selected or navigated; no day is in the tab order.
props.busy: The host is loading data: days dim and cannot be selected, keyboard focus still moves. Sets aria-busy on the grid.
props.highlightToday: Marks today, the current month and the current year visually, in the appearance’s own way. Off by default: today then looks like any other day. aria-current="date" is set on today either way.
props.disableViews: Turns the month and year views off; the header title becomes plain text. Off by default, because open-ended dates such as birthdates need the views.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla. A form passes data.appearance (or the field’s own) through the structure.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.showToday: Shows the Today button. On by default. Off removes it; the title and the month buttons stay exactly where they were.
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. Scales cells, type, gaps and default width (300–500px). md equals no size; lg and xl keep a larger minimum width.

events.dateChange: Detail { value: YYYY-MM-DD }. Fires on every user selection — a day, or the Today button when today is selectable — including re-selecting the current value; never for a disabled day or when a host sets value.
events.monthChange: Detail { month, firstDate, lastDate }. Fires whenever the days view shows another month, except when the host sets month. Use it to load that month’s data.
events.viewChange: Detail { view: days | months | years }. Fires when the view changes. Switching views never changes value.

methods.setFocus: Moves focus to the item in the tab order of the current view.

parts.header: Row holding the month heading and the controls.
parts.heading: The header title, rolling on every month and view change.
parts.nav: The Today, previous and next buttons, at the end of the header.
parts.today: Today button: selects today (value, dateChange) and shows its month; when today is disabled by a rule it only navigates and focuses. Its label shows whenever the header has room for it, otherwise the icon alone with the same accessible name. Disabled when today is outside min/max; removed with showToday false.
parts.day: Every day cell. State parts are added beside it: day-outside, day-selected, day-today, day-disabled, day-closed.
parts.day-outside: A day of the neighbouring month (muted, not selectable).
parts.day-disabled: Any day that cannot be selected.
parts.day-closed: A day ruled out by disabledDates, disabledWeekdays or isDateDisabled (struck through).
parts.day-number: The day number inside a cell.
parts.badge: The dayMeta badge inside a cell.
parts.month-button: The month, after the year; opens the months view. Rolls only when the month changes. Disabled when min and max fall in the same month, or with disableViews.
parts.year-button: The year, first in the header (inline start in RTL); opens the years view. Rolls only when the year changes. Disabled when min and max fall in the same year, or with disableViews.
parts.month: A month in the months view. States beside it: month-selected, month-today, month-disabled.
parts.month-selected: The month shown in the days view.
parts.year: A year in the years view. States beside it: year-selected, year-today, year-disabled.
parts.year-selected: The year shown in the days view.

cssProperties.--shift-calendar-badge-shift: Spacing · how far the number rises for a badge
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-border-width: Shape · cell and button border width
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-button-gap: Spacing · between icon and label in a button
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-day-line: Colour · day cell outline at rest
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-day-max-inline-size: Size · widest a day cell may get
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-day-radius: Shape · day and month cell radius
cssProperties.--shift-calendar-day-round: Shape · 1 makes day cells circles, 0 fills the column

notes: Takes the times of one day in and gives one out; it makes no requests. Times are HH:mm on a 24-hour clock whatever hourCycle shows.
Times sit in as many columns as fit (84px or wider at md), each at least 44px tall, so a narrow host gets fewer columns, never a scrollbar.

Selection follows Enter, Space or a click, not focus: arrows move focus only and pass over disabled times, so moving through the day with the keyboard never picks one. This is the documented difference from the WAI-ARIA radio group, where arrows also check.

When the times change, the outgoing grid fades while the incoming times rise one after another, and the height moves to the new row count on grid-template-rows. Loading shows skeletonCount placeholders the size of a time. Instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-time-slots-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline. The component never sets --shift-* itself.
Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku, loaded by the package’s global script.

props.times: The day’s times as HH:mm: an array, or a comma, space or JSON-array string. Sorted and de-duplicated; anything else is ignored.
props.value: The chosen time, HH:mm, or empty. Set by a pick; a host may set it (no event). A value not in times selects nothing.
props.disabledTimes: Times shown but not selectable, same shapes as times.
props.hourCycle: h23 (default) shows 09:00 and 13:00; h12 shows 9:00 AM and 1:00 PM with the language’s own AM and PM.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Sets direction, digits, the AM and PM words and the messages.
props.numerals: latn or arab. Default by language: Arabic-Indic digits for ar and ku, Latin for en and ru.
props.label: Accessible name for the group. Default: the localized word for times.
props.emptyText: Text when there are no times. Default: a localized “no times available on this day”.
props.loading: Shows placeholders instead of times and sets aria-busy while the host loads the day.
props.skeletonCount: How many placeholders loading shows (1–48). Default 8, one to two rows in most hosts.
props.disabled: No time can be chosen and none is in the tab order.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. Scales the times, type and gaps. md equals no size.

events.timeChange: Detail { value: HH:mm }. Fires on every pick, including the current value again; never for a disabled time or when a host sets value.

methods.setFocus: Moves focus to the time in the tab order.

parts.grid: The grid of times, or of placeholders while loading.
parts.time: Every time. States beside it: time-selected, time-disabled.
parts.time-disabled: A time that cannot be chosen.
parts.empty: The message shown when there are no times.

cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-chip-height: Size · smallest time height (the touch target)
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-empty-padding-block: Spacing · space above and below the empty message
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-focus-halo: Colour · halo around a focused time
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-focus-ring-offset: Focus · gap between a time and its ring
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-min-column: Size · narrowest column; as many columns as fit
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-on-accent: Colour · text on the selected time
cssProperties.--shift-time-slots-rise-distance: Motion · how far arriving times rise

owns: times of the chosen day, in the same box

notes: One request per branch, from today: the endpoint’s booking delay counts from the request’s from date, so the field never pages forward. The days shown are whatever the response holds; days without times are dropped.
calendarApiVersion picks the ids: v1 sends the branch’s Integration IDs, v2 its hash IDs, under the same query names. calendarApi must be that version’s endpoint. Default v1.

Responses are cached per branch, department, brand, version, language and day for the page’s lifetime; errors are not cached and nothing retries on its own. A stale request is cancelled when the branch changes.
The submitted value and the slotChange detail are exactly branch-slot-picker’s: value YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, detail { date, raw, value } with raw as the endpoint sent it.

States: idle (no branch yet), loading, ready, empty (no times at the branch) and error (with Try again). No day is chosen on load; the calendar opens on the month of the first open day. A new branch, or the ids going idle, returns to the days and clears the choice. Reopening a day keeps the chosen time when that day has it, otherwise clears it.

Two views in one box: picking an open day switches from the days to that day's times, the header rolling from the month to the day and the content sliding toward the start (mirrored in RTL). Change date or Escape reverses it. The box keeps the calendar's size in both views and every state; a long day scrolls inside it. Nothing below the field moves: the status row has a fixed height and also carries the validation message.
Inside the field the calendar always fills the box; --shift-booking-calendar-max-inline-size and -min-inline-size set its width.
appearance, colorScheme and size pass to the calendar and the times; host --shift-* variables reach both, since they inherit.

props.calendarApi: Full URL of the calendar endpoint for calendarApiVersion, e.g. …/api/public/calendar (v1) or …/api/public/v2/calendar (v2).
props.calendarApiVersion: v1 (default) or v2: which kind of company and branch id the endpoint takes. The host passes the matching ids; branchIds() in ~lib/booking-availability builds them from a company-branch record.
props.companyId: Company id of the branch. The field stays idle until company, branch, department and brand are all set.
props.departmentId: Department Integration ID, e.g. showroom or service-center.
props.today: YYYY-MM-DD that stands in for today: the request starts here. Empty: the visitor’s local date.
props.disabledWeekdays: Weekdays the deployment never books, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday, on top of what the endpoint returns.
props.disabledDates: One-off dates the deployment does not book, YYYY-MM-DD.
props.slotCounts: Shows each open day’s number of times as a badge.
props.hourCycle: h23 (default) or h12, for the times.
props.name: Field name in the form. Default bookingCalendar.
props.form: JS property only. The form hook; omit it standalone and listen to slotChange.
props.label: Field label. A form’s localization label wins.
props.isRequired: Required. A form hook’s own required rule applies as well.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Direction, names, digits and messages.
props.localization: Per-language label and require texts, as every form field takes.
props.defaultValue: A slot as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm: its day is chosen and that time marked when the branch has it; the field still opens on the days. Submitted as is until something is picked.
props.wrapperClass: Extra class on the field’s root.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. Scales the times, type and gaps. md equals no size.

events.slotChange: Detail { date: YYYY-MM-DD, raw: the endpoint’s text, value: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm }, identical to branch-slot-picker. Fires when a time is picked, and when a reopened day keeps the chosen time.

methods.refresh: Loads the branch again; the page cache still answers a request it already holds.
methods.setFocus: Moves focus into the view on screen: the calendar's day, or the times.

parts.label: The field label.
parts.box: The fixed box holding both views.
parts.times: The times view, laid over the calendar.
parts.times-heading: The chosen day in the header.
parts.times-time: The chosen time beside the day.
parts.times-body: The region holding the times; scrolls when a day has many.
parts.status: The row under the box: what to do next, the chosen slot, why there is nothing to choose, or the validation message.
parts.status-text: The text in the status row. status-error sits beside it on the error message.
parts.status-error: The load error text in the status row.
parts.error: The validation message, in the status row.

cssProperties.--shift-booking-calendar-back-padding-in: Spacing · Change date button side padding

owns: portaled panel holding the slotted content
appearance and colour scheme of the panel

notes: The content is slotted: the children of shift-popover move into a shift-popover-panel element that shift-portal appends to <body>, so no overflow or stacking context on the page clips them. Keep references to your content elements; do not look them up inside the popover after it loads. Children added later move too.

The panel receives the popover’s appearance, color-scheme and size attributes and its classes. It inherits nothing from where the popover sits, so set --shift-* variables on :root or on a class you give the popover.

Positioning: below the anchor, aligned to its inline start (its right edge in RTL, from the anchor’s computed direction); above when there is no room below. It never covers the anchor: when neither side has room it takes the larger side and caps its height to it, and the content scrolls inside the panel. Shifted sideways to stay 8px inside the viewport; re-placed on scroll of any ancestor, on resize and when the anchor or the content resizes. It never scrolls the page. When the anchor scrolls out of sight the panel closes.
Under 600px of viewport width the panel is a bottom sheet: full width, at most 82dvh, sliding up from the bottom edge.

Dismissal: pointer-down outside the panel and the anchor, Escape (focus returns to the anchor), Tab out of the panel (Shift+Tab from its first control returns to the anchor; Tab from its last moves to the control after the anchor), focus moving to any element that is neither the anchor nor a popover panel, and hide() from the content, for example after a date is chosen.

Focus on open: content with a setFocus() method (shift-calendar has one) is asked to focus itself; otherwise the first control in the content gets focus. show({ focus: false }) leaves focus where it is.
Wire a separate trigger button to toggle(): the pointer-down on it closes an open panel and the click that follows is ignored, so the button closes rather than reopens.

A non-modal popup (WAI-ARIA APG): the body-level shift-popover-panel element is the role=dialog and carries the id. On the anchor the popover sets aria-haspopup=dialog, and aria-controls pointing at that id whenever the anchor is in the document tree (an anchor inside a shadow root gets none, because an IDREF cannot cross the shadow boundary). It never sets or changes the anchor’s role: aria-expanded is set only when the anchor’s role allows it (a button, a combobox, or an element whose implicit role is button), so a foreign input that manages its own ARIA, such as a MudBlazor field, keeps it. shift-input’s own date input is a combobox. What the popover set is removed when the anchor changes.

The dialog always has a name: label; else, when the anchor is in the document tree and has a name of its own, aria-labelledby. For a form control (input, textarea, select) it points at the control’s name sources, never at the control, whose value would become the name: its aria-labelledby ids, else its <label> elements, except that when any label wraps the control the dialog gets the labels’ text as aria-label, with the control’s own contribution left out; a control with only aria-label gives the dialog that text, refreshed on every show(). Any other anchor, such as a button, is referenced itself. Ids the popover adds are removed again on cleanup. Otherwise the anchor’s aria-label or label text; else the localized “Pop-up”.

Several popovers can be open at once. show() on one closes another only when both share the same anchor, and focus moving into another popover’s panel does not close this one. A pointer-down outside a panel and its anchor still closes it.

Open grows and fades from the anchor edge, the sheet slides up; closing reverses. One duration, --shift-popover-settle (or --shift-settle), 320ms by default; instant under prefers-reduced-motion. The panel is position: fixed and never shifts the page layout.

The panel draws the chrome: surface, border, radius and panel shadow from the appearance. A shift-calendar in it draws none of its own and takes its size’s width; the page can still override both. minimal has no opaque surface or panel shadow in appearances.css; the panel fills them from the form-appearances guide until the shared tokens carry them.

props.anchor: The element the panel hangs from, or a CSS selector (looked up in the popover’s own tree, then the document). Any element on the page, including an input that is not ours.
props.open: Whether the panel is open. Reflected and mutable. Set it, or use show(), hide() and toggle().
props.label: Accessible name of the dialog. Without it the dialog is named after its anchor, else “Pop-up” in language.
props.offset: Gap between the anchor and the panel, in pixels. 8 by default.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. md equals no size.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Language of the default dialog name.

events.openChange: Detail { open }. Fires whenever the panel opens or closes: by method, by attribute or by dismissal.

methods.show: Opens the panel and focuses the content. show({ focus: false }) leaves focus where it is. Called while open, it moves focus into the content.
methods.hide: Closes the panel. Focus inside the panel returns to the anchor.
methods.toggle: Opens or closes the panel. Ignored for the click that follows a pointer-down which just dismissed it.

parts.panel: The portaled panel. Style it as shift-popover-panel::part(panel), or through a class given to the popover.
parts.sheet: State part beside panel while it is a bottom sheet (viewport under 600px).

cssProperties.--shift-popover-ease: Motion · easing of open and close
cssProperties.--shift-popover-lift: Motion · how far the panel travels as it opens
cssProperties.--shift-popover-scale: Motion · scale the panel grows from
cssProperties.--shift-popover-settle: Motion · duration of open and close
cssProperties.--shift-popover-sheet-max-block-size: Size · tallest the bottom sheet may get
cssProperties.--shift-popover-width: Size · panel width; the content’s own width by default
cssProperties.--shift-popover-z-index: Other · stacking order of the panel

owns: field rendering: label, control, prefix and suffix slots, clear, hint and error

notes: One element, one type at a time: text and date now. Each type is a module (types/<type>) that says how a value is shown, how typed text is read back, and what the type adds to the control; a new type adds a module, not a change to the field.

A form field (FormElement): subscribes to form under name, reports value through getValue(), resets to defaultValue, takes required, disabled and error state from the form, and adds a check to the field’s schema that fails while typed text is refused. Standalone it stands on isRequired, isDisabled and errorMessage.
Typed text is read on blur and Enter, never while typing; valueChange fires when the committed value changes.

type="date": value is YYYY-MM-DD or empty. The input shows it in format (default dd/MM/yyyy; tokens d, dd, M, MM, yyyy with any separators) and reads the format with any separators, eight digits in format order, or YYYY-MM-DD; Arabic-Indic digits are read as Latin. An impossible date, one outside min/max and one a rule closes leave the value empty and show a localized message; localization[language].format, .minMessage, .maxMessage ($minDate$, $maxDate$) and .unavailableMessage replace them.

type="date": the calendar button, Alt+ArrowDown and a click in the input (openOnControlClick) open a shift-popover holding shift-calendar, anchored to the input. A click leaves focus in the input so typing continues; the button and Alt+ArrowDown move focus to the selected day, else today, else the first day that can be chosen. Choosing a day writes the value and closes; Escape closes without changing it.

type="date": every shift-calendar prop passes through from one list (types/date/calendar-pass-through.ts): value, month, min, max, enabledDates, disabledDates, disabledWeekdays, isDateDisabled, dayMeta, today, highlightToday, weekStartsOn, numerals, disableViews, showToday, busy, disabled (from isDisabled), label, language, appearance, colorScheme, size.

The support line under the control is reserved in every state and holds the hint or the error, which cross-fade in it, so a message never moves anything below the field. A long message in a narrow field may wrap onto a second line.

Appearance, colour scheme, size and fonts as shift-calendar. The guide gives material and minimal no border: material is the filled text field (muted fill, square bottom corners, an underline that thickens and turns the focus colour on focus), minimal an underline with a muted label. These control tokens are local until appearances.css carries them. Classes on the field travel to its calendar panel.

props.name: Field name, reflected so the form finds the field. Required inside a form.
props.value: The committed value: text as typed, or YYYY-MM-DD for date. Reflected and mutable.
props.defaultValue: Initial value, and what reset() returns to.
props.label: Field label. Inside a form the structure’s localized label wins.
props.placeholder: Input placeholder. Default for date: the format written with localized letters, e.g. dd/mm/yyyy.
props.hint: A line of help under the control, in the reserved support line. The error takes its place while there is one.
props.isRequired: Marks the field required when used standalone; inside a form the schema decides.
props.readonly: The value can be read and selected but not changed; no clear and no calendar.
props.clearable: Shows a clear button while there is a value. Off by default.
props.autocomplete: The input’s autocomplete. Off by default.
props.inputmode: The input’s inputmode. Default by type: text, or numeric for date.
props.errorMessage: An error to show when used standalone. Typed-entry and form errors take precedence.
props.form: The FormHook that owns the field. Omit it for standalone use and listen to valueChange.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Sets direction, labels and messages, and the calendar’s language.
props.localization: Per-language overrides: { [lang]: { label, placeholder, hint, require, format, minMessage, maxMessage, unavailableMessage } }.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. md equals no size.
props.format: type="date": display and typing format. Default dd/MM/yyyy. Tokens d, dd, M, MM, yyyy in any order with any separators; anything else falls back to the default.
props.openOnControlClick: type="date": open the calendar when the input is clicked. On by default.
props.month: Month the calendar opens on, YYYY-MM. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.min: Earliest date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD; earlier typed dates are refused. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.max: Latest date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD; later typed dates are refused. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.enabledDates: Allow-list of YYYY-MM-DD. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.disabledDates: Dates that cannot be chosen or typed. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.disabledWeekdays: Weekdays that cannot be chosen or typed, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.isDateDisabled: JS property only. (date) => boolean for any other rule. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.dayMeta: Per-day badge, tone and description keyed by YYYY-MM-DD. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.today: YYYY-MM-DD that stands in for today. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.highlightToday: Marks today visually. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.weekStartsOn: First weekday column, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.numerals: latn or arab digits in the calendar. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.disableViews: Turns the calendar’s month and year views off. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.showToday: Shows the calendar’s Today button. Passed to the calendar (type="date").
props.busy: The host is loading availability: days dim and cannot be chosen. Passed to the calendar (type="date").

events.valueChange: Detail { value }. Fires when the committed value changes: typed text read on blur or Enter, a day chosen, or cleared. Empty when typed text is refused.
events.inputBlur: The input lost focus, after typed text was read.
events.monthChange: type="date": the calendar’s monthChange, forwarded. Detail { month, firstDate, lastDate }.

parts.label: The label.
parts.required: The required mark inside the label.
parts.control: The box holding prefix, input and suffix; carries the border and the focus ring.
parts.prefix: The prefix slot’s box, before the input.
parts.input: The text input. For type="date" it is a combobox that opens the calendar.
parts.suffix: The box after the input: clear, the type’s buttons and the suffix slot.
parts.calendar-button: type="date": the button that opens the calendar.
parts.hint: The hint, in the reserved support line.
parts.error: The error, in the reserved support line.

cssProperties.--shift-input-button-gap: Spacing · between buttons in the suffix
cssProperties.--shift-input-danger: Colour · error border, message and required mark
cssProperties.--shift-input-focus-halo: Colour · halo around the focused control
cssProperties.--shift-input-focus-outline-width: Focus · outline ring width (0 for material, whose underline shows focus)
cssProperties.--shift-input-focus-ring-offset: Focus · gap between the control and its ring
cssProperties.--shift-input-line-strong: Colour · control border on hover, and the underline
cssProperties.--shift-input-muted: Colour · placeholder, hint and prefix/suffix text
cssProperties.--shift-input-radius-end: Shape · bottom corner radius (0 for material and minimal)
cssProperties.--shift-input-support-gap: Spacing · between the control and the support line
cssProperties.--shift-input-underline-width: Shape · underline width (material and minimal); doubled on focus

notes: The day-strip counterpart of shift-calendar: the same inputs, the same dateChange, a horizontal row of day cards instead of a month grid. It makes no requests and knows nothing about branches or times.

Which days appear: min to max. When enabledDates is set and an end of the range is missing, that end is the first or last enabled date; with neither, 30 days from today (or the 30 days ending at max, when max is before today). A min later than max shows no days.
At most 366 days are rendered, counted from the first day of the range. Later days are not shown and cannot be selected; a value among them selects no card.

Rule precedence is shift-calendar’s, through the same library: range (min/max) → disabledDates → disabledWeekdays → not in enabledDates → isDateDisabled. Blocked days stay visible as disabled cards (data-reason names the rule); rules only ever block.

Semantics: a horizontal listbox of options (WAI-ARIA APG listbox), not a radiogroup, because the arrow keys move focus without selecting and Enter or Space selects; a radiogroup checks the radio the arrows land on. One card is in the tab order (roving tabindex): the selected day, else today, else the first open day. Disabled days are focusable with aria-disabled so they can be discovered.

Moving focus, setting value and the previous/next buttons scroll the strip only, never the page or an overflow: hidden ancestor. On first render the selected card is placed without animation; later changes scroll smoothly (instantly under prefers-reduced-motion). Scrolling snaps per card; touch swipe and trackpad scroll natively.
The previous and next buttons scroll by one visible page and are disabled at the ends. The edge fades grow with the distance scrolled, so they appear only where content continues.

The strip’s height never changes with selection, month labels, badges, highlightToday or the colour scheme; only another size, another density (appearance), the caption row, or the phone layout below a 600px viewport (roomier cards, as in the booking prototype) changes it.

Appearance and colour scheme follow .shift form-appearances: every value resolves as --shift-day-strip-x, then --shift-x, then the appearance, then the vanilla baseline, so host variables win in light and dark. The component never sets --shift-* itself.

Fonts: Nunito (vanilla, material, soft) or Manrope (sharp, minimal), with Noto Kufi Arabic first for ar and ku — all loaded by the package’s global script. Override with --shift-font-family and --shift-font-family-arabic.

props.value: Selected date as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty. Updated when the user selects a day; a host may set it, and the strip scrolls to it.
props.min: First day shown and earliest selectable date (inclusive).
props.max: Last day shown and latest selectable date (inclusive).
props.disabledDates: Dates that cannot be chosen: an array or a comma, space or JSON-array string of YYYY-MM-DD. They stay visible, disabled.
props.disabledWeekdays: Weekdays that cannot be chosen, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday: [5, 6], "5,6", "5 6" or "[5,6]".
props.enabledDates: Allow-list. When set (any array, even an empty one) only these dates can be chosen; without min or max it also sets the first or last day shown. Null, undefined or an empty string turns it off.
props.isDateDisabled: JS property only. (date) => boolean for any other rule; asked only about days no other rule blocked. A throw counts as disabled.
props.dayMeta: Per-day extras keyed by YYYY-MM-DD: { badge?: short text, tone?: neutral | info | success | warning | danger, description?: read with the date by screen readers }. The badge sits beside the month label under the number. Object or JSON string.
props.today: YYYY-MM-DD that stands in for today, through ~lib/clock. Empty: the reader’s local calendar date.
props.language: en, ar, ku or ru. Sets names, direction and digits.
props.numerals: latn or arab. Default by language: Arabic-Indic digits for ar and ku, Latin for en and ru.
props.label: Accessible name of the listbox (the field label when used in a form). Default: the localized “Choose a day”.
props.caption: Short text above the strip, at its end, such as “15 days available”. Empty by default, and the row is shut. Content in the caption slot takes its place. The listbox is described by it.
props.disabled: Nothing can be selected or paged with the buttons; no card is in the tab order.
props.busy: The host is loading data: cards dim and cannot be selected, keyboard focus still moves. Sets aria-busy on the listbox.
props.highlightToday: Marks today visually, in the appearance’s own way. Off by default; aria-current="date" is set on today either way.
props.appearance: vanilla, material, soft, sharp or minimal. Unset renders vanilla. A form passes data.appearance (or the field’s own) through the structure.
props.colorScheme: light (default), dark, or auto (follows prefers-color-scheme; for hosts that are themselves dark-aware).
props.size: xs, sm, md (default), lg or xl. Scales the cards, type, gaps and buttons. md equals no size.

events.dateChange: Detail { value: YYYY-MM-DD }. Fires on every user selection, including re-selecting the current value; never for a disabled day or when a host sets value.

methods.setFocus: Moves focus to the card in the tab order and scrolls the strip to it.

parts.root: The whole strip: the caption row and the row of buttons and cards.
parts.caption: The caption above the strip (caption prop or caption slot).
parts.prev: Previous-page button, at the inline start. Disabled at the start.
parts.next: Next-page button, at the inline end. Disabled at the end.
parts.viewport: The scrolling, snapping box that clips the cards and carries the edge fades.
parts.day: Every day card. State parts are added beside it: day-selected, day-today, day-disabled, day-closed.
parts.day-disabled: Any day that cannot be selected.
parts.day-closed: A day ruled out by disabledDates, disabledWeekdays or isDateDisabled (struck through in vanilla and sharp).
parts.weekday: The weekday abbreviation at the top of a card.
parts.month: The month label, on the first card and on each first of the month.
parts.badge: The dayMeta badge, beside the month label.

cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-blocked-border-style: Shape · unavailable card border style (dashed by default)
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-blocked-decoration: Type · closed day number decoration (e.g. line-through)
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-border-width: Shape · card and button border width
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-caption-gap: Spacing · between the caption and the cards
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-cell-size: Size · density unit; a card is 1.45 of it wide
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-day-padding-inline: Spacing · card padding at the sides
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-day-row-gap: Spacing · between the lines of a card
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-fade: Size · edge fade width; a scrolled card comes to rest just inside it
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-focus-halo: Colour · halo around a focused button
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-focus-inner: Colour · band inside a card’s focus ring
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-focus-ring-offset: Focus · gap between a button and its ring
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-label-font-size: Type · weekday and month label size
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-label-line-height: Type · weekday and month label line height
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-nav-gap: Spacing · between the buttons and the cards
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-on-accent: Colour · text on the selected card
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-shadow-room: Spacing · room below the cards for their shadow (20px in soft, else the hover lift)
cssProperties.--shift-day-strip-today-mark-stroke: Today · text stroke that bolds the number
